title: Another account on the machine can call decade's MCP tools
body:
decade serves its MCP tools over streamable HTTP on `127.0.0.1`, at a port the kernel picks (`start` in `decade/src/server/mcp.rs`). Programs decade starts get the address in `DECADE_MCP`, as `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/mcp?workspace=<id>`, with `&pane=<name>` added for a program in a pane. `Decade::call_tool` takes the workspace and the pane from the query string and checks nothing else.

Every account on the machine can connect to a loopback TCP port. Workspace ids are small integers, and a scan of local ports finds the server. A caller from another account can then use every tool as an agent would:

- `scratch.open` runs any program on decade's `PATH`, with any arguments, as the user who runs decade.
- `screenshot` returns a pane's image at once when the pane is in accept screenshots mode. Otherwise it puts the consent dialog in front of the person.
- `scratch.send`, `show`, `highlight` and `point` act on the person's panes.

On a machine with one user this exposes nothing. On a shared machine it lets another user run code as the person who runs decade.

## Options

| option | cost |
|---|---|
| a random token in the URL | decade makes a secret at start, puts it in `DECADE_MCP`, and refuses any request without it. Harnesses keep working, because they use the URL as given. |
| a unix socket in a `0700` directory | Only the owner can connect. Harnesses that accept only an HTTP URL cannot reach it, and coax hands the server to its agent as a URL in the ACP session's server list. |

I lean to the token. It closes the hole without changing what harnesses must support.

## Open

- `docs/protocol.md` documents the address as ending in `?workspace=<id>`. Programs pass the address along without reading it, but a new query parameter still changes the documented form. Is that a protocol change under the versioning rules?
close_reason: Dropped: decade runs only on machines with one user account, so no other account can reach the loopback port.
